t: Core Principles of Persistent Shared Virtual Worlds
title: Core Principles of Persistent Shared Virtual Worlds
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Four principles govern persistent shared virtual worlds. Principle 1: the audience experience is the product: technology serves the story, not the reverse. Principle 2: consistency builds worlds: characters, rules, and lore must hold together. Principle 3: human direction stays central: tools amplify creators, they do not replace judgment. Principle 4: craft is measurable: quality bar is set by the work, verified by audiences. The piece records show where each principle is enforced in hardware and software.

t: Key Vocabulary of Persistent Shared Virtual Worlds
title: Key Vocabulary of Persistent Shared Virtual Worlds
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Six terms unlock the whole database. real-time rendering: generating imagery fast enough for interactive experience. procedural generation: creating content algorithmically from rules and seeds. continuity: keeping story facts consistent across scenes and episodes. volumetric display: showing true three-dimensional imagery. haptics: technology conveying touch and force feedback. interactive narrative: stories that respond to audience choices. The glossary program below looks up any of these terms instantly; use it while reading the other records.

t: How the Pieces of Persistent Shared Virtual Worlds Fit Together
title: How the Pieces of Persistent Shared Virtual Worlds Fit Together
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Eight pieces make persistent shared virtual worlds: Creative Direction System, Asset Generation, Real-Time Engine, Narrative Logic, Audio Production, Distribution Platform, Audience Interface, Rights and Attribution. This record is the integration map — how they connect, in what order they are built and tested, how data and control flow between them, and what the system does when a piece fails. The architecture follows a simple rule: each piece owns one job completely, interfaces are narrow and documented, and the system is tested as a system, not just as eight passing pieces. Read this record after the piece records and before the build plan.

t: Build Plan: Making Persistent Shared Virtual Worlds Step by Step
title: Build Plan: Making Persistent Shared Virtual Worlds Step by Step
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: From parts to working system, in order: Stage 1: Creative Direction System — holding the artistic vision consistent across everything produced Stage 2: Asset Generation — characters, worlds, props, and sounds created or curated Stage 3: Real-Time Engine — rendering and interaction running at full fidelity Stage 4: Narrative Logic — story structure, branching, and continuity management Stage 5: Audio Production — music, dialogue, and effects mixed for the experience Stage 6: Distribution Platform — delivering the work to audiences on their devices Stage 7: Audience Interface — how people participate, play, and interact Stage 8: Rights and Attribution — crediting creators and respecting ownership Each stage ends with a verification gate — the tests in the corresponding piece record — and the next stage does not start until the gate passes. This sequencing is the difference between a pile of parts and a system: integration risk is retired early, when it is cheap to fix, not late, when it is expensive. Budget time for the gates; they are the work, not overhead.
key_points: Stage 1: Creative Direction System — holding the artistic vision consistent across everything produced
Stage 2: Asset Generation — characters, worlds, props, and sounds created or curated
